MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  FEBRUARY 20, 2024

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A special meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 7:00 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers, 4045
  Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR BAIN.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR BAIN led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Persichina,  Holdsworth,  Johnson,
  McCormick and Bain

  Commissioners Absent:  Ciarolla

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REORGANIZATION PRESENTATION

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the City Council appointed
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK as Chair and COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA as
  Vice Chair of the COMMISSION.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN was recognized for her service as 2023 Chair of the
  Commission and was provided a plaque for her service.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY
  16, 2024

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the word “ride” was missing after the word
  “Mayor’s” on page 4 in Item 8B.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
February 20, 2024
   APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  JANUARY 16, 2024 WITH THE CORRECTION ON PAGE 4.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  2024 SUMMER MOVIE NIGHTS PROGRAM

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the 2024 Summer Movie Nights
  Program (as per the agenda material).

  The Commission discussed the movies to show at the June and July movie nights
  and decided on the movies “Migration” and “Elemental” as the two to be shown.

  B.  2024 COMMITTEE, SUBCOMMITTEE, ADOPT-A-PARK ASSIGNMENTS

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the proposed Commissioner
  committee, subcommittee, and adopt-a-park assignments for the upcoming year
  (2024). He noted the preferences of Commissioner Ciarolla who was absent from
  the meeting.

  A discussion ensued among the Commission about the proposed assignments.
  They coordinated amongst themselves with the assistance of Staff the assignments
  that they would like to hold for 2024.

  C.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS LIST

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave an overview of the capital improvement projects list
  (as per the agenda material).

  Commissioner Bain asked what a prioritized list would look like with the listed
  projects. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that if he could prioritize a project it
  would be the drainage improvements at the Tennis Center project.

  Supervisor Pinuelas clarified that Staff does ask for the input of the Commission
  with capital improvement projects regarding the priority of the current projects or if
  the Commission would like to consider any other projects that were not listed, in
  response to Commissioner Bain.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
February 20, 2024
   Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the assessment of potential spaces for a dog park
  was listed as a future project and could be considered in a future fiscal year budget,
  in response to VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that funds are allocated annually for ADA projects and
  the next project that is being considered is near Chandler Park, in response to
  COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that it was recommended that benches be added to
  different areas of City Hall after the turf renovation project. Superintendent
  Goldsmith added that benches have been considered in the two flat gravel areas,
  in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that Staff is looking to have more secured trash
  receptacles in certain areas of Highridge Park as well as having a receptacle with
  an organic waste component, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if the grading of the grass areas at Ernie Howlett Park
  would be considered as a future project. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that this
  would be a costly project and could be considered as a future project.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that Staff is waiting on City Hall camera assessment to
  consider moving forward with security cameras in other park areas, in response to
  CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH stated that the first phase of Founders Park
  project and the drainage project at the Tennis Center should be prioritized projects.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that she agreed that fixed trash receptacles were a
  good idea for Highridge Park but was unsure how successful an organic waste
  receptacle would be at the park.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON concurred that any project like correcting drainage
  issues and tree trimming that emphasized correcting a possible safety issue should
  be prioritized. Superintendent Goldsmith noted that the tree trimming above the
  fitness equipment at Ernie Howlett Park is due to keeping the equipment clean.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested adding additional fitness equipment along the
  Pagliano Pathway at Ernie Howlett Park as a future project.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Equestrian Committee will also have the
  opportunity to add any projects to the list that may be a part of the equestrian arenas
  and trails, in response to VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
February 20, 2024
   Superintendent Goldsmith noted that Staff has made a reduction in water use
  throughout the City and that there is nothing new that is being considered for water
  conservation projects at this time, in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  D.  RECREATION FEE REVIEW

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the Rolling Hills Estates recreation
  fees (as per the agenda material).

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the tennis club members would be notified of
  the fee increases. He noted that there was some push back in the past when the
  City made a large increase in the fees but stated that he did not see any issue with
  the proposed fee increases. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that Staff will be sending
  out the standard letter to the tennis club members but will look into whether a letter
  was sent out earlier when fees have been increased.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that she did not believe that the increase in the
  tournament fees would cover the costs of the tournament, but Staff could look into
  what the cost would need to be per doubles team to cover the cost of the
  tournament, in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  Supervisor Pinuelas clarified that USTA charges fees for each team registration for
  the Doubles Tournament and Staff builds in the fees to the registration fee on the
  USTA website to cover the fees recouped by USTA, in response to
  COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  ACCEPT STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION TO THE NEW RECREATION
  FEES STRUCTURE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  **ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING AT 7:40
  PM**

  E.  ADVISORY BOARD REVIEW OF PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ANNUAL
  REPORT

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the Pepper Tree Foundation Annual
  Report for Advisory Board review (as per the agenda material).

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff had
  not started the naming rights at the Nature Center donations and will begin
  marketing those opportunities soon and at some of the upcoming events.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
February 20, 2024
   **RECONVENE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING AT 7:45 PM**

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING SCHEDULE
  CHANGE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief update on the change to the regular meeting
  schedule from the third Monday of the month to the third Tuesday of the month.
  She noted that the future meeting dates on the third Tuesday of the month were
  included in the agenda packet.

  B.  FOUNDERS PARK UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas shared that bids for the first phase of Founders Park are due
  on February 22 and Staff will update the Commission as more information becomes
  available.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN reported that at Highridge Park there are some small
  weeds growing in certain areas. She also noted that there has been some runoff of
  the mulch in those areas of the park. She also stated that she was able to speak to
  some dog owners at the park who had some dogs off leash, and they respectfully
  listened to her and placed their dogs on leash. She asked if there could be some
  more dogs on leash signs placed around the park. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that
  Staff is in the process of ordering signs. COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked if there
  was a fee for the violation of these certain dogs off leash codes. Supervisor
  Pinuelas stated that there is a fee involved for violating municipal codes, but it is a
  process. COMMISSIONER JOHNSON suggested that adding verbiage on the
  signs about the possible penalty may help in deterring violations. Supervisor
  Pinuelas informed the Commission that Code Enforcement has been over to
  Highridge Park at different times and has reported back that he has not seen a lot
  of activity of dog off leash at the park.

  COMMISSIONER POPE reported that at Highridge Park there was a broken bench
  near the first base side dugout.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
February 20, 2024
   COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH reported that at Rockbluff Park he alerted
  Superintendent Goldsmith of a broken tree branch that broke a section of a fence.
  He also noted that there has been some trail erosion at the park.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that his maintenance staff monitors and inspects
  the trails after a major rain event but also relies on the local equestrians to report
  any issues to him which is a huge assistance, in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR MCCORMICK asked whether Staff could gather information about the
  utilization of the pickleball courts at the Tennis Center at Ernie Howlett Park.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that it was just added as a future agenda item and staff
  will be reporting back this information at a future meeting.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN provided an update regarding leaf blower use and policy
  considerations regarding electric and gas leaf blowers from the last Environmental
  Advisory Committee meeting.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 23, 2024
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 23, 2024 SPECIAL MEETING
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  SECURITY CAMERA PROJECT UPDATE

  NONE

  B.  PICKLEBALL UPDATE

  NONE

  C.  ASSESSMENT OF SPACE FOR POTENTIAL DOG PARK AND FUTURE PARKS

  NONE

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
February 20, 2024
   CHAIR MCCORMICK ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:55 PM TO THE NEXT
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON MARCH 19, 2024, AT 7:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CITY HALL.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Ryan McCormick
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
February 20, 2024
